I’m happy to walk you through what the request would look like—just keep your API key out of public posts!  
Below is a **template** you can copy into `curl`, Postman, or a short script. Replace `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with *your* key before running:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

IP="12.234.56.126"
LIMIT=10          # maximum results per page
CURSOR="pointer"   # set this to whatever value you got from a previous response, otherwise omit

BASE_URL="https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3"

# Build the URL – add &cursor=<value> only when CURSOR isn’t empty
if [[ -n "$CURSOR" ]]; then
    ENDPOINT="/ip_addresses/${IP}/files?limit=${LIMIT}&cursor=${CURSOR}"
else
    ENDPOINT="/ip_addresses/${IP}/files?limit=${LIMIT}"
fi

FULL_URL="${BASE_URL}${ENDPOINT}"

echo "Requesting ${FULL_URL}"
curl --silent \
     -H "x-apikey: <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
     "${FULL_URL}" > vt_ip_files.json

echo "Response written to vt_ip_files.json"
```

### What each part does

| Piece | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `/api/v3` | Base path for VT v3 REST endpoints |
| `/ip_addresses/<IP>/files` | Endpoint that lists all files that communicated with the given IP |
| `?limit=` | How many items you want back (max 1000, here we cap at 10) |
| `&cursor=` | Pagination token returned in a prior result (`next_cursor`) |

#### Example JSON snippet (simplified)

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "_id": "abcd1234",
      "attributes": { ... }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "links": {
    "self": "...",
    "next": "?cursor=XYZ..."
  },
  "meta": {
    "page_info": {
      "total_results": 42,
      "results_per_page": 10
    }
  }
}
```

If there are more than ten matches, the `"links.next"` field will contain another cursor value (`XYZ…`). You’d repeat the same request replacing `CURSOR` with that new value until `"links.next"` disappears.

---

#### Quick‑start with Python (requests)

```python
import os
import requests

url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP}/files"
params = {"limit": LIMIT}
headers = {"x-apikey": "<YOUR_API_KEY>"}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())
```

Just swap in your own values and hit “Run”.

Feel free to let me know if you hit any hiccups while wiring up the call!
